diffs.diff: pin count: part has 6 (GND 5V SDA SCL IN+ IN-), datasheet reading has 4 (GND 5V SDA SCL)
diffs.evidence: The second reading listed only the 4-pin Grove PinMap; the exact product (U013) also ships a 2-pin screw terminal for the measured voltage, '1 x HT3.96 Male Socket (2 pins)', which is the + / - input that the M5Stack Arduino example describes as 'Use ADC Unit to convert 0 ~ 12V analog voltage', so IN+ and IN- are real pins.

diffs.diff: voltage_V: datasheet reading gives 0.0000625 per count, the part's model has 0.0004028, 0.0008057
diffs.evidence: The M5Stack UiFlow driver for U013 converts at the terminal with 'voltage = ((value / (-1 * min_code.get(self._rate) * self._gain)) * 3.3) * 4' using 'min_code = {8: -32768, 16: -16384, 32: -8192, 128: -2048}', i.e. 13.2/32768 = 0.0004028 V per count at 8 SPS (config 0x9C) and 13.2/16384 = 0.0008057 at 16 SPS (config 0x98, TI DR bits '1                   0                 16SPS'); the model's 0x98 response wrongly used the 128 SPS scale (0.006445) and was fixed, while 0.0000625 (2.048 V/32768) is not an ADS1100 step at all since its reference is VDD and ignores the unit's divide-by-4 input.
